body:
Some variations of the issue:
- Window set to exclusive fullscreen.  Goes to windowed mode.
- Window set to exclusive fullscreen.  Goes borderless fullscreen.  Sometimes mouse is misaligned with UI.
- Window set to exclusive fullscreen.  Goes to borderless fullscreen.  Offsets window so it's no longer centered.
- Window set to exclusive fullscreen.  Goes to windowed, but has no border.  Changing setting between fullscreen and windowed does not bring the window border back.

I've been experiencing this a lot lately.

Just a bit more info when I've got it stuck in this state:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f17fed48-a205-4353-a25f-6a2cb46e5e73)

It's behaving like fullscreen, but the mouse input for the UI is offset.  When I alt-tab, you can see the game window offset, as I have screenshotted here.  I can mouse over the UI here and it's correct.  Bringing the game back in focus makes it "fullscreen" again, but the settings menu doesn't seem to think it's fullscreen or borderless fullscreen.

get_tree().root.mode is 0 (MODE_WINDOWED), but clearly the game is not windowed.  Don't think I ever had issues like this with Godot 3, which had a bunch of separate booleans for windowed/borderless/maximized/etc. instead of one enum.  I think the enum is getting out of sync with what state the window is actually in.

Also, the desktop window manager on Windows 10 is going absolutely bonkers and eating up every last bit of GPU when Godot is in this state, really lagging my computer.  Not sure if one is causing the other.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5287c0b5-58a6-4d32-8117-ca1598fdacd6)

Another bit of info -- it seems there are 2 windows when launching:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79b26fe9-a74a-42ef-9591-ec3e07c5fd25)

Note how there's a maximized window in the background and a smaller window in front.  The backround one is correct -- the game should have been launching in maximized mode, however, the one in the back gets closed and the smaller foreground window is what's used.  It seems as if Godot creates a window on init, then removes that window and creates a new one, and if you apply settings too soon, they apply to the first window?  Not really sure why the second window is created.

This is launching from the editor.  Not sure if this happens in release builds.

Edit: Also, for further clarification, I'm using a viewport width and height of 1920x1080 in windowed mode with a width and height override of 800x600, then in _ready() of an autoload, I load a config file and set fullscreen/maximized/etc. based on a config file.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bedc44f1-b737-4e06-88c2-143192421f83)

Trying to get all the info I can when this happens.  If anybody has suggestions for other things to test, let me know.  I tried printing out the window flags when this occurs:
Borderless flag is false
Borderless boolean is false
Exclusive is false

Though that's the same when I set it to exclusive fullscreen and it's working properly.  I would have expected the exclusive flag to be true in this case?
